_comment: Ground-truth eval set for sample_docs/sample_return_policy.pdf. expected_keywords are checked case-insensitively against the generated answer (ANY-of per group is not required — ALL groups should ideally be hit; coverage is reported as a fraction, not pass/fail, since exact LLM phrasing varies). expected_source is checked against the filenames of retrieved chunks for retrieval-metric scoring (hit rate / MRR).

cases.question: What is the return window for most items?
cases.note: Tests whether an exact number survives retrieval+generation. BM25 should help here since '10 days' is a literal token.

cases.question: How many days do I have to return a laptop?
cases.note: Requires distinguishing the electronics-specific window (7 days) from the general one (10 days) - a common RAG failure mode is answering with the wrong number from a nearby sentence.

cases.question: How long does it take to get my money back after returning something?
cases.note: No literal keyword overlap with the source phrasing ('refunds are processed within') - tests semantic/vector retrieval, not just BM25.

cases.question: It's been 5 days since I returned my item, when will I get my refund?
cases.note: Mirrors the worked example in the QA prompt: the model must not refuse just because 'my item' isn't in the docs - it should answer the general refund-timeline policy.

cases.question: How soon do I need to report a damaged or defective item?
What items are not eligible for a refund?
cases.note: Tests whether the model lists multiple items from an enumerated clause rather than picking just one.

cases.question: If I paid cash on delivery, how do I get refunded?
What can I do if my refund hasn't arrived after 10 business days of approval?
What is ShopMart's CEO's name?
cases.note: Negative test: nothing in the document answers this. The model should say it can't find the information, not hallucinate a name.

cases.question: My laptop broke after the return window closed, what are my options?
cases.note: Requires connecting the return-window clause with the separate warranty clause - tests whether retrieval pulls back both relevant chunks.
